$comment: Who answers for each robot account (non-human identity) in the lab tenant, and why (ADR 0018, nhi-standard N1: at least two human owners - a named owner plus a backup).

Owners are ADMIN accounts (lab/iga/admin-accounts.json), never a workforce account, never break-glass. An Entra owner can add a credential to the app and act AS it, so ownership is power, not a label: the rules below decide who may hold it.

Rule 1 (ADR 0018 Consequences): owners of a Tier-0 identity must be Tier-0 people. A standing owner of a Tier-0 identity holds Tier-0 power with no PIM activation, which contradicts ADR 0020's zero standing access ('no admin keeps power when they are not using it'). So the Tier-0 rows name no owner until the lead decides (the build account already holds standing Global Administrator, so it is the one owner that adds no new reach).
Rule 2 (SOD-08, lab/iga/sod-rules.json): the access governance lead certifies access, so she never owns an identity that can create, change or disable accounts.

Where each list lives: 'terraform' rows are set by code (envs/dev TF_APP_OWNER_OBJECT_IDS for modules/apps; envs/bootstrap pipeline_owner_object_ids; envs/operator operator_owner_object_ids) - an owner added in the portal is removed by the next apply. 'post-apply' rows are set once by the operator with the Graph calls in postApplyStep and read back.

Checked by lab/scripts/powershell/06-NHI-Inventory.ps1 (EnabledHumanOwners per row; OWNER-NONE / OWNER-NO-HUMAN / OWNER-SINGLE findings). Object ids are not kept here: resolve an admin account with GET /users/<upn>?$select=id.

identities.why: Sign-in and account creation in AWS for staff; no Graph permission. Its owners can change its claims and assignments, which ADR 0018 accepts for a named owner.
Staff sign-in to the IT help desk; no Graph permission.
Creates and switches off ServiceNow accounts from App-ServiceNow-Users; no Graph permission.
The clinical portal's sign-in and app roles; no Graph application permission.
Entra as the identity provider for the acquired clinic's Okta; delegated sign-in scopes only.
Read-only Graph plus create-only writes to the WORM evidence container.

identities.kind: app registration made by Entra device registration (2026-10-29, when vm-win11-01 joined)
identities.why: Holds no permission and no credential; it lives in this tenant, so the inventory counts it, and someone must answer for it.
Uploads HR rows that create and disable workforce accounts. SOD-08 keeps the access governance lead off it; the only other human without a conflict is the build account (lead's decision).

identities.managedBy: terraform: envs/bootstrap pipeline_owner_object_ids.hr_provisioning (one azuread_application_owner per person; HR-SYNC stays an owner for .OwnedBy)
identities.why: Its job creates and disables workforce accounts in AD: same reasoning as HR-SYNC.

identities.kind: Cloud Sync configuration app (AD to Entra)
identities.why: Its sync job writes every synced workforce account into Entra (the work of the Tier-0 Hybrid Identity Administrator role): same reasoning as HR-SYNC.

Read-only Graph, but it reads the envs/dev Terraform state, which holds the generated break-glass passwords (envs/bootstrap main.tf, 'Remote state'): whoever can act as PLAN can sign in as a Global Administrator. Rule 1.

outOfScope.what: Managed identities: vm-win11-01, vm-dc01, id-kv-idlab-reader, pb-identity-contain, pb-identity-notify
outOfScope.why: Entra has no owners for a managed identity; it lives and dies with its Azure resource, and who controls it is Azure RBAC on that resource (the inventory's OwnerModel 'Azure RBAC on the resource').

outOfScope.what: Vendor apps: Microsoft Graph Command Line Tools, O365 LinkedIn Connection
outOfScope.why: Multi-tenant apps registered in Microsoft's own tenants (publisher Microsoft): their owners are the publisher. This tenant governs them through consent (ADR 0018 consent policy), not ownership.
Owned and run by Microsoft; the inventory counts them and leaves them out.

postApplyStep.add: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/applications/{app object id}/owners/$ref and, where the app has one, POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/servicePrincipals/{sp object id}/owners/$ref, body {"@odata.id": "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/directoryObjects/{admin account object id}"}
postApplyStep.docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/application-post-owners and .../serviceprincipal-post-owners: app-only needs Application.ReadWrite.All + Directory.Read.All (Learn: Application.ReadWrite.OwnedBy is not sufficient to add another owner)
